site.title: Hannune — Applied AI Systems Under Real Constraints
site.description: Hannune is a solo technology company focused on designing and stabilizing AI systems that must operate reliably beyond demos, under real-world constraints.

hero.title: AI systems that must keep working after deployment
hero.subtitle: When demos succeed but reality introduces constraints, trade-offs, and responsibility.

content.intro: Hannune is a solo technology practice built around a simple idea: some AI systems fail not because models are weak, but because architectural decisions break under real-world constraints.

subsections.title: Identity
subsections.intro: Hannune focuses on problems where systems must continue operating after deployment, not just during demonstrations.
points: Designed for situations where operational responsibility matters
Works best when constraints shape architecture decisions
Not a dev shop or ticket-based implementation service
Single decision-maker with end-to-end system context

structure.heading: Operating Model
structure.description: Solo by design — centralized responsibility, consistent technical judgment

subsections.title: How It Works
subsections.intro: Hannune operates at the boundary between what AI can do in demonstrations and what it must do in production. The focus is not on building features, but on making systems that remain operable, understandable, and stable after handoff.

patterns.title: Constraint-driven environments
items: Cloud usage restricted by policy or cost
Data privacy requirements preventing external APIs
Systems expected to run continuously without manual intervention

patterns.title: Long-running agent systems
items: Agent workflows that work in demos but fail in production
Unclear ownership of agent behavior after deployment
Operational instability under real usage patterns
Need for predictable behavior over benchmark performance

patterns.title: Production integration realities
items: Existing infrastructure that cannot be replaced
Legacy systems interacting with modern AI components
Trade-offs between reliability, cost, and capability

subsections.title: Decisions & Systems
subsections.intro: Examples of architectural decisions made under real constraints. These are not portfolio pieces but illustrations of how trade-offs were navigated.

cases.title: Local-first Agent System
cases.description: Designed a local-first agent system where cloud APIs were restricted and operational stability mattered more than model benchmarks. Key decisions focused on predictable behavior, failure isolation, and long-term maintainability.

cases.title: LLM Infrastructure Under Cost Constraints
cases.description: Migrated LLM workloads from cloud APIs to local infrastructure under strict cost constraints. The focus was not cost reduction alone, but ensuring the system remained operable and understandable after deployment.

content.intro: Hannune is not a general-purpose service. Clarity about fit helps both sides avoid wasted effort.

fit.heading: When Hannune is a good fit
fit.description: Hannune works best when AI systems have moved beyond prototypes and must operate reliably under real constraints, with clear ownership expectations.

nonfit.heading: When Hannune may not be a fit
nonfit.description: Projects seeking rapid feature delivery, advisory-only engagement, or experimentation without long-term responsibility may be better served elsewhere.

content.intro: If your system works in demos but becomes uncertain after deployment, an initial conversation may help clarify where constraints and responsibility truly lie.
